Own Intent-to-Buy and Propensity-to-Buy scoring models across solutions and segments, including inputs, logic, validation against closed outcomes, and ongoing recalibration
Bring public sector signal sources, including procurement activity, grant awards, and audit and compliance data, into the scoring models and test whether each one predicts conversion
Define and enforce account and contact data standards for prospect and target accounts, driving remediation with GTM Systems rather than stopping at the report
Analyze win rate, sales cycle, churn, and expansion patterns by segment and vertical to sharpen the ICP and translate findings into targeting rules the field can execute
Own competitive intelligence across segments and solutions, including win/loss patterns and FOIA-sourced commercial insight
Partner with Sales, BD, and Marketing to operationalize scoring and segmentation into territory views, prioritized target lists, and outbound workflows
What You Bring
You have 4+ years in go-to-market analytics, revenue operations, market intelligence, or a comparable analytical function
You have built, maintained, or evaluated an account or propensity scoring model and can speak to how it was validated and what you changed based on evidence
You bring strong Salesforce capability, including reporting and a working understanding of the account, contact, and opportunity data model
You are fluent in advanced Excel or Google Sheets and comfortable working with large, messy, multi-source datasets
You can explain a model's logic, its limits, and its results clearly to non-technical sellers and leaders
 Nice-to-Have Qualifications
Familiarity with public sector procurement cycles, budget data, or the GovTech market
Experience managing enrichment or intent data vendor relationships, including ingestion logic and refresh cadence
Hands-on experience with SQL and one or more BI tools such as Tableau, Power BI, or Looker
Practical use of AI tooling for research, enrichment, or unstructured data analysis
Location
This position will be hybrid with 3 days/week in our[Oakville, ON office.

Role Overview
 The Sales Compensation Business Partner, MXRM is the dedicated compensation partner for approximately 500 MXRM GTM professionals globally, spanning Specialized Sales, Pre-Sales / PDEs, Services sellers, sales management, and partner/channel roles. The role brings focused ownership to work currently split between the Head of MXRM GRO and in-zone GTM Operations teams without dedicated compensation expertise.
The role is the single point of accountability inside MXRM across the compensation year—from quota setting through plan rollout, seller questions, mid-year changes, reporting and year-end payout queries. It connects field needs with the central DISW compensation function, resolving what can be handled locally and escalating clear, well-framed cases when needed.
This is a senior individual-contributor role with no direct reports. Influence comes from compensation expertise, sound judgment and credibility with sellers, country managers and the central compensation team. The position is designed as a full-year role: October–January quota setting is the peak cycle, supported by year-round governance, analytics, enablement and plan-effectiveness work.
 Key Responsibilities
 Quota Setting Process (October–January)
Own the end-to-end MXRM quota-setting process for Pre-Sales / PDEs, Services sellers, Specialized Sales and sales management. Partner with Country Managers, who set individual seller quotas, to validate country-level coverage against targets, reconcile aggregates, issue PCTs on time and ensure sellers have signed plans before the fiscal year opens. This is the role’s highest-value and highest-visibility annual deliverable.
 Compensation Plan Rollout & Enablement
Lead the field-facing annual plan rollout: translate approved designs into clear communications, deliver enablement by role and zone, publish supporting materials and help the organization understand plan mechanics before payouts begin. When plans change, explain both what is changing and why.
 Voice of MXRM in Compensation Strategy
Represent MXRM in compensation-design discussions with the central DISW Compensation team, bringing the Specialized Sales perspective upstream rather than after plans are finalized. Make evidence-based cases where corporate defaults do not fit MXRM’s GTM motions, including ARR / NRR priorities, Land-to-Expand and a high-velocity funnel; document MXRM requests and track outcomes.
 First Line of Defence — Seller Compensation Queries
Serve as the single MXRM point of contact for questions about payouts, deal credit and plan-rule application. Resolve issues locally where possible; escalate structured, well-framed cases to the central team when necessary. Provide a dependable support path for sellers while reducing avoidable load on the Head of MXRM GRO, in-zone Operations and central Compensation.
 Governance of Mid-Year Seller Changes
Govern compensation-related handling of role moves, territory splits, transfers, hires and leavers. Ensure account-team membership, LAER crediting setup and SAP Commissions configuration are updated so transactions can be credited correctly. Establish systemic data-hygiene controls and return actionable fixes to field owners; this is not transaction-by-transaction policing.
 Compensation Performance Reporting
Deliver a standing monthly / quarterly compensation view for MXRM leadership, covering payout analytics, attainment distribution, outliers, potential under- or overpayment flags, and FSO consolidation and submission to central compensation administrators. Build a concise management view and respond to material Country Manager requests.
 Compensation Plan Effectiveness Analysis
Evaluate whether plan mechanics and incentives drove intended behavior. Identify gaming patterns and areas where rewards may not align with desired outcomes; provide a credible evidence base for the next fiscal-year plan-design cycle and the role’s MXRM advocacy.
 SPIF / Incentive Program Design & Tracking
Design, track and close out MXRM-focused SPIFs, accelerators and contests tied to specific commercial objectives. Partner with central Compensation on structure and compliance; own MXRM execution, commun

uding attainment, coverage, pipeline-versus-quota and account-team / LAER data-hygiene checks.

Company Overview
 Docusign brings agreements to life. More than 1.8 million customers and more than a billion people in over 180 countries use Docusign solutions to accelerate the process of doing business and simplify people’s lives. With intelligent agreement management, Docusign unleashes business-critical data that is trapped inside of documents. Until now, these were disconnected from business systems of record, costing businesses time, money, and opportunity. Using the Docusign AI-native IAM platform, companies can create, commit, and manage agreements with solutions created by the #1 company in e-signature and contract lifecycle management (CLM).
What you'll do
As a Senior Sales Compensation Analyst (P3), you will drive the day-to-day global sales compensation administration process, with a core focus on managing the end-to-end setup and maintenance of eligible employees in Xactly Incent. You will own the support of your assigned population's commission calculations, addressing sales inquiries, performing meticulous audits, and responding to regional inquiries. You will collaborate cross-functionally with Sales Operations, Finance, HR and Legal to review the accuracy and completeness of new participant setups, manage plan mechanics, and support the monthly commission cycle. You are a self-sufficient, out-of-the-box thinker and team player focused on resolving a wide range of operational challenges, scaling existing processes, and consistently meeting critical corporate deadlines.
This position is an individual contributor role reporting to the Manager, Sales Compensation.
 Responsibility
Manage the monthly set-up process and administration parameters within Xactly Incent, including the active management and maintenance of Users, People, Position, Hierarchy, Named Relationships, Quotas, and Guarantees
Administer the full sales compensation lifecycle, including the monthly review of sales participant setups, crediting/commission audits, and the timely resolution of field inquiries via ServiceNow
Troubleshoot set-up issues by partnering closely with the Administration team
Collaborate with the Systems team to automate the set-up process by integrating to WD, while continuing to coordinate manual processes, corrections, and exceptions on a monthly or quarterly basis
Train the Sales Organization on Xactly, Sales Plans, and new Sales Compensation programs
Conduct rigorous User Acceptance Testing (UAT) for fiscal year plan rollovers and mid-year compensation plan modifications to maintain system integrity
Understand data mining, systems, and order processes to create data models that help produce analysis and identify trends or gaps, maintaining monthly reporting and ad hoc analysis
Evaluate and responsibly adopt technical tools and AI solutions to optimize workflows, automate manual gaps, and boost overall team productivity
Govern internal controls and maintain business workflows to ensure 100% compliance with SOX requirements and operational audit standards
Partner with the Sales Plan Design team to prep the launch of Sales Plans and T's and C's, and work directly with Sales Leadership to provide localized coaching and ad-hoc support for communicating compensation outcomes
Job Designation
 Hybrid: Employee divides their time between in-office and remote work. Access to an office location is required. (Frequency: Minimum 2 days per week; may vary by team but will be weekly in-office expectation)

What you bring
 Basic
Bachelor's degree in Finance, Business, or a related field
5+ years of experience in sales compensation administration and incentive tracking systems
 Preferred
Experience with Xactly or similar Sales Performance Management (SPM) software
Experience handling sales incentive plans within the technology, SaaS, or AI sectors
Analytical skills and strong business acumen
Proficiency in MS Office Suite and Google Workspace
Strong communication, documentation, organization, and presentation skills
Life at Docusign
 Working here
 Docusign is committed to building trust and making the world more agreeable for our employees, customers and the communities in which we live and work. You can count on us to listen, be honest, and try our best to do what’s right, every day. At Docusign, everything is equal.
We each have a responsibility to ensure every team member has an equal opportunity to succeed, to be heard, to exchange ideas openly, to build lasting relationships, and to do the work of their life. Best of all, you will be able to feel deep pride in the work you do, because your contribution helps us make the world better than we found it. And for that, you’ll be loved by us, our customers, and the world in which we live.

 About Zen Educate
 Zen Educate is a technology company that matches schools with temporary educator staff. Our mission is to change the world of education recruitment. Schools spend over $9bn a year on temporary educators, with over $2bn per year of that spent on fees that take money out of the education system. By leveraging the latest technology, we purpose built a platform that helps schools to pay less while educators earn more.
We want students to have access to the best education possible, and we go the extra mile to find, onboard, match, and coach incredible educators that deeply care about their students. We wake up every day on a mission to care more. We care more about our schools. And we care more about our educators.
We have recently raised our Series B funding of $37mil, the largest round in European EdTech last year. This is an exciting opportunity to make a difference and be part of a high growth start-up that is expanding rapidly in the UK and US markets!
 Why this role exists
 Zen Educate places educators in K-12 schools across :20 US regions. Behind every new partnership sits operational work that has to be done right: RFP submissions with tight deadlines and long compliance checklists, hectic conference seasons with significant logistical and planning requirements, nuanced district contracting processes that need to be managed with care and attention.
As Zen has grown, so has the volume of this work, and we're investing in RevOps capacity to match. That gives us room to run each process well and to keep raising the bar on it: every RFP, conference and contract is a chance to make the next one faster and more automated while holding the same standard of polish and accuracy.
This role takes ownership of the critical operational tasks RevOps supports today, and is accountable for how each one turns out. You'll learn each process by running it yourself, which is how you'll see where it breaks and which steps can be automated. Then you'll build those automations, so the work gets faster and more reliable each cycle and frees you to take on the next area. RFPs, conferences and deal desk are where you start. As those run well, the role grows into other parts of RevOps where the same approach pays off.
 What You'll Own
 Your first priorities are below. Each one has a direct line to how quickly Zen signs and launches new partnerships, and they're where RevOps support is most stretched today. Expect the list to change as your automations take work off your plate and new areas need an owner.
 RFP submission coordination. You'll own Zen's RFP process from the moment a bid is identified through submission, and early on it will take the largest share of your time. That means understanding what each district is asking for and what it takes to be compliant, building responses from our existing content, and bringing in subject matter experts across sales, operations, compliance and finance where a question needs something new. You set the plan, keep contributors on it, and make sure what goes out is complete and compelling. The quality of what goes out decides whether we win, so each bid should leave our content library and process in better shape for the next one.
 Conference and event coordination . Our sales team attends state and national education conferences throughout the year, and they're some of the best chances reps get to meet district decision makers in person. Once an event is on the calendar, you own setting the team up to make the most of it. That covers logistics (registration, booth and sponsorship, shipping, travel, spend against the events budget) and the work around them: pulling attendee lists, supporting the coordination and planning of tertiary events around the conference, collaborating with marketing sponsorships that put us in front of the right people, and making sure every key progress with conference attendees is logged in Hubspot following the event.

About Wolt
 At Wolt, we create technology that brings joy, simplicity and earnings to the neighborhoods of the world. In 2014 we started with delivery of restaurant food. Now we’re building the delivery of (almost) everything and you’ll find us in over 500 cities in 30 countries around the world. In 2022 we joined forces with DoorDash and together we keep on dreaming big and expanding across the globe.
Working at Wolt isn’t always easy, but it’s definitely exciting. Here you’ll learn more, build more, and ship more than in most other companies. You’ll be challenged a lot, but also have a lot of fun on the way. So, if you’re a self-starter with drive and entrepreneurial spirit, this could be the ride of your life.
 About The Role
 Wolt is on a growth journey as part of the DoorDash family, together with Deliveroo. Drive is our delivery-as-a-service business: we let merchants offer fast, reliable delivery in their own channels (their webshop, app or ordering system), powered by the Wolt and Deliveroo courier networks. We're now bringing Drive across Wolt and Deliveroo countries together into one EMEA business , with one team and a clear ambition: grow fast and build a business that stands on its own feet.
A growing share of that scaling comes from outside restaurants: grocers, retailers, pharmacies and other eComm players who want on-demand and same-day delivery for their own customers. Their needs can be very different from restaurants: bigger baskets, scheduled and batched deliveries, larger and heavier items, longer distances and more complex integrations. This brings us to you, our next Manager, Strategy & Operations for Grocery & Retail Drive.
You'll own this segment across EMEA, from strategy and planning to pricing, product requirements and performance. You'll work hand in hand with our regional commercial teams, who own the partner relationships, and with Product, Logistics, Finance and our Marketplace grocery & retail teams. You'll join the Drive EMEA Strategy & Operations team and report to the Director of Strategy & Operations, Drive EMEA.
 What You'll Be Doing
Own the Grocery & Retail strategy and annual plan for Drive EMEA: where we play, which partners we go after, and the growth and profitability we commit to.
Set the commercial framework for the segment, including pricing guidelines, deal economics and investment cases for our largest partnerships, together with the regional commercial leads.
Act as the voice of grocery and retail partners towards Product and Logistics, turning commercial needs such as scheduled delivery or large and heavy items into sized, prioritized requirements.
Run performance management for the segment: track growth, unit economics and service levels for our biggest partners, spot what's off and drive the fix with the teams involved.
Shape how Drive works with our Marketplace grocery & retail teams, so partners get one joined-up offer from us.
Turn wins into playbooks that country teams can reuse, from the first pitch to launch and scale-up.
 Our humble expectations
5+ years of experience in strategy & operations, business development, commercial roles or management consulting, with a track record of owning outcomes, not just recommendations.
Strong commercial and analytical skills: you can build a deal P&L or a segment plan from scratch, and defend it in front of a partner's leadership or our own.
Proven ability to get things done across a matrix organization without direct authority, working with regional teams, Product, Logistics and Finance.
You use AI tools (e.g. Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini) in your daily work, for example in analysis, planning and ways of working, and look for new ways to apply them to elevate you - whilst maintaining strong judgement that comes from personal understanding complex systems
Structured thinking and clear, concise communication in English, both written and spoken.
Willingness to travel occasionally across our EMEA markets.
 Seen as a strong advantage:
Background in retail, grocery, e-commerce, logistics or on-demand delivery, either in-house or advising companies in these sectors.
Experience with B2B platform or delivery-as-a-service businesses.
 Why you'll love it
🚀 Global and growing fast: Be part of a fast-moving business at the moment it's being built, across two of Europe's best-known delivery brands
🛒 A segment to own: Work with some of the biggest grocery and retail brands in Europe, and see what you write end up on the product roadmap
🤩 Ride of a lifetime: Accelerate your career with direct access to DoorDash's global Drive experience and room to grow as the segment scales
💪 Instant impact: Take ownership and make a difference
💙 Big hearts and small egos: Surround yourself with smart, friendly people
 Next steps
 If you are excited about working in a high-growth environment, taking ownership, and being part of an extremely ambitious team, then click below to apply, make sure to add your CV in English and get the conversation going! We will be reviewing applications on a rolling basis.
Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion
We’re committed to growing and empowering a more inclusive community within our company, industry, and cities. That’s why we hire and cultivate diverse teams of people from all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We believe that true innovation happens when everyone has room at the table and the tools, resources, and opportunity to excel.
 Beware of recruitment scams: DoorDash, Deliveroo, and Wolt will never ask you to pay money or share sensitive financial information during hiring — learn more about our legitimate recruiting process at Recruitment Scam Awareness - DoorDash .

 XPENG is a leading technology company focused on designing, developing, manufacturing, and marketing intelligent mobility solutions, including electric vehicles (EVs), electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) aircraft, and robotics. About PingPong 
PingPong is on a mission to simplify global growth for businesses. With $200B+ in payments processed, we're one of the world's leading cross-border payments platforms, and we're just getting started.
We have 32 offices in 11 countries and over 1,500 employees, helping businesses solve complex payment needs in every major economy and across all time zones.
 Location: London
 The Role 
We're looking for a Senior Associate in Revenue Operations & Enablement to help our Business Development team across Europe & the Americas sell faster and smarter.
You'll sit at the centre of our commercial engine: equipping BDs with the knowledge, training and tools they need to win, supporting them on live deals, and keeping our CRM, performance and commission reporting accurate. You'll work closely with BD leadership, Finance, Compliance and Product.
You'll be our first dedicated Revenue Operations & Enablement hire, trusted to set your own priorities and run with them independently, so you won't just run processes, you'll play a key part in designing them. If you like turning messy, manual work into clean systems that a growing team relies on, this role is for you.
 What You'll Do 
 BD enablement and training: Build and maintain our BD knowledge hub (product guides, pricing, pitch materials, RFP responses, competitor insight). Design and run onboarding for new BDs and ongoing training as our products and markets evolve, and track whether it's working.
 Performance and commission: Track BD performance against targets, including pipeline, conversion and revenue. Handle BD commission queries, and help refine commission plans and incentives as we grow.
 CRM ownership: Be the day-to-day owner of our CRM (HubSpot). Keep pipeline data clean and consistent, set data standards, and build the dashboards BD leadership uses to run the business.
 Process building: Spot what's manual, broken or missing in how the team sells or deals are implemented, then design and roll out better processes, playbooks and automations as the team scales.
 What You'll Bring 
3–5 years of experience in sales enablement, revenue operations or sales operations, ideally in payments, fintech or financial services.
A track record of building enablement content or training for commercial teams, such as playbooks, product guides or onboarding programmes.
Hands-on experience with CRM and sales enablement tools (e.g. HubSpot, Salesforce, Apollo, Clay), including reporting and data hygiene.
Strong analytical skills and advanced Excel skills; experience with data and business intelligence tools is a plus.
Experience administering commission plans or sales incentive schemes.
A self-starter mindset: you spot what needs fixing and build the process to fix it, without waiting to be asked.
Highly organised, with the ability to juggle competing priorities effectively.
Excellent communication skills, written and spoken, and the confidence to run effective training sessions and push back on BDs when standards slip.
 Why Join Us 
Real ownership: you'll shape a function early, not inherit one.
A small, hands-on team where your impact is visible from day one.
Direct exposure to commercial leadership and the deals that drive our growth in Europe & the Americas.

 Read more about what we’re building here .

We're looking for a commercially driven Go-To-Market leader to own how Treatwell takes its products to market across Europe. Working closely with our sales teams and leaders, and with Product, you'll turn our roadmap into revenue, with a particular focus on growing our financial services product line.
At Treatwell we don't just sell software: we help Europe's best salons and spas digitalise their business, grow their revenue and improve the experience they offer their clients.
You'll be the strategic owner of go-to-market for Treatwell across Europe. With a strong commercial mindset and a highly collaborative approach, you'll define how we position, price, package and launch our products, and partner with Sales to turn them into real, measurable revenue.
 You Will Be Responsible For
Commercial go-to-market strategy: Own and lead Treatwell's European go-to-market strategy, defining target segments, positioning, pricing, packaging and commercial priorities, with a clear focus on revenue growth.
Financial services revenue: Own and lead projects that drive revenue for the financial services product line, from payments to new financial solutions, setting clear targets and taking accountability for results.
Sales partnership: Work closely with our sales teams and sales leaders across markets to shape commercial plans and targets, and turn go-to-market strategy into pipeline, deals and revenue.
Sales enablement & playbooks: Build scalable playbooks, pricing guidance, sales narratives and training that help local market teams sell our products and drive adoption on the ground.
Product launches: Partner with Product to bring new products and features to market, from validation and pilots through to full European rollout, bringing the commercial and customer perspective into the roadmap.
Product-led growth: Alongside our sales teams, build in-app and self-serve sales motions that help adoption and revenue scale efficiently.
Cross-functional leadership: Partner with Product, Supply, Finance, Operations, Legal and local market teams to embed payments into acquisition, onboarding, account management and retention.
Strategy into execution: Translate strategy into clear execution plans with owners, timelines and KPIs, proactively removing blockers and driving accountability across teams that don't report directly into the role.
Commercial performance & optimisation: Track and drive adoption, revenue and margin across markets, using data and customer insight to optimise pricing, packaging and the sales funnel.
Stripe partnership: Manage Treatwell's strategic partnership with Stripe, acting as the senior commercial point of contact and aligning joint go-to-market plans and growth priorities.
 About You
Proven experience in go-to-market, commercial strategy or sales strategy roles within a fast-growing digital or tech company (marketplaces, SaaS, delivery, fintech or similar)
Strong commercial focus, with a track record of owning revenue targets and driving measurable growth
Multi-market experience is a must: you've worked closely with sales teams and sales leadership across multiple markets
Experience leading commercial strategy across multiple markets, ideally in a central or group-level role
Strong analytical skills and confidence building business cases, commercial models and senior leadership updates
Excellent stakeholder management and the ability to influence and drive accountability without direct authority
Exposure to payments, fintech or embedded finance products is a plus
 About Treatwell
 We're a team of 800+ people working every day to transform the beauty industry across Europe. We've built the leading salon management software, connected to Europe's number one marketplace, helping thousands of professionals run and grow their business.
 The Numbers Speak For Themselves
Over 95,000 partner salons
Present in 14 countries
More than 23.5 million bookings every year
And the best is yet to come. If you want to join an international, innovative and fast-growing company where your work has a real, visible impact... join us!
 We'll Treat You With
 💰Compensation: A competitive base salary and bonus package.
🌍Location & flexibility: Based in London, Milan or Amsterdam, working closely with teams across all our European markets.
💻Work tools: All the tools and technology you need to do your best work.
🚀Impact: A rare opportunity to build and own a new growth engine for Treatwell from the ground up.
 Salary : €90K - €140K (depending on experience)
 Equal opportunities
 At Treatwell we're committed every day to creating and maintaining an inclusive workplace, built on mutual respect and valuing everyone's uniqueness. We offer equal opportunities to all our candidates and employees, without any form of discrimination.

Description
 Reporting to the President, Mitchel Lincoln/SVP Quebec Atlantic Packaging, the Director, Sales Operations (Corporate) is responsible for owning, standardizing, and continuously improving the commercial operating system across the organization. This is a corporate role working in collaboration with all sales regions in the Atlantic Packaging network (Ontario, Quebec, USA).
This role does not own sales targets nor manage sales teams directly. Instead, it enables Sales Leadership and P&L owners to execute consistently by providing clear processes, disciplined governance, and effective tools.
The role addresses recurring structural issues in sales execution (contracts, risk exposure, forecast visibility, onboarding effectiveness, and CRM adoption) and brings process excellence to an area historically driven by individual experience rather than system discipline. Sales Operations builds the system so Sales / Marketing / Legal / Finance / CX work together efficiently.
 Success Factors in the Role
 Success in this role will be judged on system outcomes, not activity.
Sales execution becomes repeatable
Fewer deal-specific workarounds; consistent deal flow through the same stages and approvals.
Sales leaders use the tools willingly
Salesforce is used because it makes running the business easier, not because it’s mandated.
Commercial risks are visible before decisions (with a disciplined reduction process)
P&L owners can see contract duration mix, terms exposure, and liability accumulation before approving deals.
Fewer “surprises”
Fewer last-minute escalations due to undocumented terms, unclear approvals, or cross‑region inconsistencies.
Improved funnel credibility
Forecast discussions are grounded in a shared, disciplined view of the pipeline.
CX feedback loop is integrated into the sales process which will result in better CX scores across the businesses
 Responsabilités
 This role sets standards and runs governance. Sales Leadership owns execution. Finance/Credit/Legal co-own approval rules and risk thresholds.
 Sales Operating Model & Governance
Own and maintain the front-end sales operating model, including:
Contract approval workflows and limits of authority (with Legal).
Clear rules when customers operate across regions.
Partner with Legal, Finance, and Credit to make risk explicit and decision-ready.
Ensure P&L leaders have visibility before commitments are made, not after.
 Salesforce Ownership
Act as business owner of Salesforce (process design, usage standards, reporting logic).
Drive adoption by defining how and why Salesforce is used:
Funnel structure aligned with business needs (product mix, seasonality, capacity).
Standard dashboards for P&L owners and Sales Leadership.
Reduce “system noise” so the tool supports decisions, not administration.
 Funnel Management & Sales Planning
Define and enforce consistent funnel management practices.
Provide forward-looking visibility on revenue concentration by:
Factory
Asset type
Industry
Salesperson
Other cuts as needed
Enable proactive capacity and production discussions (vs. reactive firefighting).
Drive development of sales plans that can be handed off for execution.
Enable consolidation of this data for the Group.
 Contract, Terms & Risk Tracking
Implement standardized reporting on:
Contract tenure mix (no contract, quarterly, annual, etc.).
Payment terms exposure.
Aggregate liability commitments.
Make commercial risk measured, visible, and discussable (not implicit or anecdotal).
 Sales Training / Motivation / Other
Design and institutionalize a formal sales onboarding and training framework.
Develop role-specific training (e.g., Salesforce usage, contract basics).
Build a repeatable cadence for sales meetings to drive consistent themes and execution.
Any other tasks, as requested by his/her manager
 Exigences
Required: Bachelor’s degree in Business, Commerce, Finance, Operations, or a related field required.
7+ years of experience in progressive experience in Sales Operations, Revenue Operations, Commercial Excellence, or Business Analytics
Expert in Salesforce, specifically in design, governance and adoption.
Strong background in Sales Operations, Commercial Excellence, or Revenue Enablement.
Comfortable influencing senior sales leaders without hierarchical authority.
Process-oriented, systems thinker with a strong business bias.
Credible with Finance, Sales, and Operations alike.
 Remarque
 The successful candidate must be bilingual (French and English), as they will be required to communicate with employees at the head office located in Ontario.
 Avis aux lecteurs

li-4489906842.description:
Team: Marketing
 Prolific
 Prolific isn’t just enabling AI innovation – we’re redefining it. While foundational AI technologies are becoming commoditized, Prolific’s human data infrastructure provides the high-quality, diverse data required to train the next generation of AI models. Through our platform, we empower researchers and companies to access a global, ethically curated participant base, ensuring cutting-edge AI research and training grounded in inclusivity and precision.
 The role
 This is a brand new role, and you’ll be the first person to do it at Prolific.
Right now, the insight that could help us win more deals is scattered. We have valuable learnings about why we win, why we lose, and why deals stall, but they aren’t turned into the pitch, proof and materials that sellers use every day. You’ll fix that. You’ll become the person who knows our market position inside out and turns it into tools that help sellers win.
This is a revenue role. It sits at the point where product marketing meets sales enablement, across both our AI and research businesses. You’ll dig into win-loss, competitive intelligence and customer proof, then turn it into pitch decks, one-pagers, battlecards, case studies and training that reps use on their next call. You’ll also help new AEs and SDRs get up to speed faster.
You’ll be measured on win rate, sales cycle length, rep ramp time and how well equipped our sellers are in front of a buyer.
Our AI PMM leads strategic lab and enterprise AI pursuits, and our vertical PMMs tailor messaging for specific audiences. You own the foundation they all build on: the shared, trusted system of resources every other deal runs on.
 What you’ll bring to the role
6+ years in an enablement-facing role (product marketing, sales enablement or competitive intelligence) at a B2B company
Experience enabling sellers across more than one product or product line, at a startup, scale-up or enterprise
Experience doing the full job, not just the final slides: you’ve gathered the data and insight yourself, then turned it into materials sellers use
Enablement you’ve built that measurably moved win rate, ramp time or deal velocity. You can show who used it and what changed
Hands-on experience running buyer interviews. You ask about past behaviour, not hypothetical opinions, and you can get a lost buyer to tell you the real reason
Comfort with data: you can pull from a CRM and call-intelligence tools, build an analysis or business case, and defend your conclusions
Clear writing for busy readers: short, specific and easy to act on
Credibility with sellers and senior leaders, and the ability to get sales, product and customer success to act without managing any of them. You’ll spend a lot of time with sales
 What you’ll be doing in the role 
Build and own sales enablement across AI and research: onboarding, ongoing training and launch readiness (with the AI PMM), plus a single source of truth that reps actually use
Audit what exists today, decide what stays and what goes, and set up a way to keep it current
Build and maintain the core sales toolkit: pitch narrative, decks, one-pagers, discovery guides, battlecards, objection handling, white papers and business-case tools
Design and run our win-loss programme: buyer interviews after closed-won, closed-lost and no-decision outcomes, combined with CRM and call data and a regular readout to leadership. You’ll also run one outreach calendar for every AI buyer interview, including the AI PMM’s, so no buyer is asked twice
Own competitive intelligence against data labelling vendors, research panel providers and in-house alternatives, including a live view of competitor pricing and positioning that feeds the AI PMM’s category point of view
Turn findings into specific changes, such as a new talk track, a revised discovery question or a pricing recommendation, then check whether the change moved the number
Own customer proof: case studies with AI and research customers, a sourced library of proof points, the reference programme for live deals, and advocacy through quotes, reviews and speakers
Sit in on sales calls every week and feed deal-level evidence into product: feature gap
[...]
RM fields for loss reasons and competitor.
 Why Prolific is a great place to work
 We've built a unique platform that connects researchers and companies with a global pool of participants, enabling the collection of high-quality, ethically sourced human behavioral data and feedback. This data is the cornerstone of developing more accurate, nuanced, and aligned AI systems.
We believe that the next leap in AI capabilities won't come solely from scaling existing models, but from integrating diverse human perspectives and behaviors into AI development. By providing this crucial human data infrastructure, Prolific is positioning itself at the forefront of the next wave of AI innovation – one that reflects the breath and the best of humanity.
Working for us will place you at the forefront of AI innovation, providing access to our unique human data platform and opportunities for groundbreaking research. Join us to enjoy a competitive salary, benefits, and remote working within our impactful, mission-driven culture.

li-4489929239.description:
Why am I looking for my first hire: 
 Demand has outgrown what my network of external delivery partners and I can handle. At the same time, my ambition is to build a consultancy firm that solves commercial challenges for SaaS & AI companies. That's why I'm hiring for this role. 
 Shortly about the company: 
I'm Nils Brosch (SaaS.eu.com B.V.), a B2B SaaS and AI sales consultant, trainer and coach. I help post-product-market-fit companies, mostly Series A and up across the Benelux and DACH, build repeatable sales processes and stronger sales teams.
Before consulting, I co-founded two software and tech companies that went on to employ more than 400 people. Over the last seven to eight years I've worked with 140+ companies on a consulting, fractional, training and coaching basis.
My approach is diagnostic first, grounded in 1,400+ manually reviewed sales calls and my own frameworks for discovery, coaching and commercial maturity.
 What you'll do: 
You'll work directly with me on client delivery and own a growing share of it yourself.
 Design trainings. Build new training programs and customise existing ones to each client's sales motion, market and team.
 Develop coaching concepts. Come up with new formats, exercises and frameworks that make coaching stick.
 Run coaching trajectories. Take over ongoing coaching for reps and frontline managers, next to my senior engagements.
 Run commercial due diligence. Dig into a client's sales process, data and calls to find where deals really get stuck.
 Prepare coaching and training delivery. Review calls, build session materials and package programs so partner trainers can run them too.
 Build the knowledge base. Turn years of training content, frameworks and research into a structured, reusable library.
You'll use AI daily to do this faster and better, and you'll design materials that look as sharp as the thinking behind them.
 Where this leads: 
This role is a launchpad. After the first phase, you grow in one of two directions, based on where your strengths and ambition point:
 Operations lead. Become the quarterback for the network of delivery partners I've built over the years: matching them to clients, running quality and keeping delivery on track.
 Consultant, coach and trainer. Step in front of the room yourself. Run diagnostics, coach reps and managers, and deliver trainings under your own name.
We'll decide the direction together, once we both know what you're great at.
 Who you are: 
You've sold, or enabled people who sell, and you can explain why something works. At the same time you stay curious about what you don't know yet.
 Must-haves 
2+ years in sales or sales enablement and you are passionate about it
Experience in a startup or scale-up of roughly 1 to 20 people, or you've been an entrepreneur yourself
Excellent English, written and spoken
Organised: you bring structure to messy content and keep many threads moving
Ambition: you see yourself leading operations or coaching & training in a few years
Curiosity: You’re always looking to sharpen your craft - whether through reading, listening to podcasts, or attending relevant meetups
 You’ll stand out if you have the following skills 
Dutch and/or German (preferred, not required)
You've coached people or facilitated trainings before
Strong design skills: you make decks, handouts and visuals that look professional without a designer
Strong AI skills: you already use AI tools to research, code, write, analyse and build, not just to summarise emails
Experience with tools like HubSpot, Miro and Google Workspace
 How we work: 
 Hours: full-time. Prefer to start part-time? Let’s discuss.
 Location: hybrid, Amsterdam based. Remote is possible in principle, but as my first hire, regular face time is essential to get things off the ground

Barden is delighted to partner with one of our clients in the software domain as they look to hire a Head of Customer Success. This is a rare chance to own the full customer journey, from the first pilot to long-term growth, at a business that is expanding. You will lead a small customer success team, stay close to customers, and shape how the business onboards, supports, retains, and grows them.

We're unlocking access to the NHS, because healthcare is not truly free until it's truly accessible 💙
 The world’s best healthcare, for free. It's not a new idea, it's called the NHS. But the largest healthcare provider is fundamentally broken. Patient satisfaction is at an all time low, and the biggest reason cited is lack of access. So we’re on a mission to fix it with technology that actually works.
We're building the front door of UK healthcare, creating a future where one billion NHS appointments are transparent and instantly bookable, and patients are guided to the right service first time using AI.
We're developing critical national infrastructure. Today, 26% of GP practices in England use our patient registration software, while one in five GP practices in London use Bookable Search to help new patients find and book appointments seamlessly.
Our latest product, Bookable Navigator, extends this vision by automatically booking appointments for existing patients.
We operate from within a working GP practice in East London 🏥 We're backed by Y Combinator, Innovate UK and the NHS Clinical Entrepreneur Programme, and were previously ranked the 8th fastest-growing startup in the UK and 33rd fastest-growing in Europe 🚀
 ⛩️ Our Principles 
 Exciting challenges lie ahead. Guided by our principles, we’ll meet these challenges with a thoughtful and caring approach. These principles drive everything we do at Healthtech-1:
💙 Care deeply
🏋️‍♀️ Work hard
🤝 Be your word
💬 Trust in radical truth and transparency
 🚀 Do your life's best work
🥳 Find the fun
Read more about our principles and our "why" in the Healthtech-1 Handbook.
 🎯 Goal expectations
 As our Special Projects Associate (GTM) , you’ll be the right-hand to our Growth Lead.
You’ll own GTM tools, systems and special projects delivery. The immediate need is to uplift reporting (revenue and performance) and CRM hygiene. Future special projects may include (but are not limited to) lead generation, sales enablement, enterprise sales support, AE onboarding, etc.
This is an exciting and varied IC role for an analytical operator who wants exposure to strategy and operations in a fast-growing GTM org. We want someone smart, detail-oriented and humble.
 🏆 Objectives in your first 90 days
 Objective 1: Uplift our systems
 You will pick up and own Attio (our CRM) as a source of truth. This means making sure our customer data is current and usable for AEs. It also means making sure we have an accurate way to report and predict our sales pipeline. You will set up Attio well, then build tooling on top of it using AI (e.g. dashboards and maps).
 Objective 2: Give the team and leadership clear visibility
 You will uplift the way we report to leadership, and within the growth team. You will build and maintain dashboards tracking revenue growth, cycle targets and product adoption. You will work with our Growth Lead on pipeline analysis. In owning this reporting work, you will have exposure to decision-making on growth strategy and performance management.
 Objective 3: Enable the growth team to sell more
 The Growth team are your customer and you will find ways to solve their problems and make them more effective! You will build and maintain quality lead lists. You will support AEs with operational queries, targets and tooling. You will build automations and workflow improvements that save them time. You will help new growth hires ramp faster.
 ⚠️ This role is not for everyone
 This is a high-ownership, high-expectation role. You'll be working in a fast-moving commercial environment where accuracy, speed, and proactivity all matter at the same time.
You probably won't enjoy this role if you:
Prefer to be told what to do over figuring out what to do
Treat ops as a support function rather than a growth lever
Aren't comfortable getting
[...]
rivate medical insurance, because we believe in the NHS and we are here to improve it!
🐥 Parental leave: Post passing probation it is: statutory - 6 weeks 90% pay then, SMP for 33 weeks; if you've been an employee for a year: 12 weeks 100% pay then, SMP for 27 weeks; and if you have been here for 2 years: 18 weeks 100% pay then, SMP for 21 weeks. This will improve over time. We also include up to £9,000 of childcare contribution for primary caregivers to support a five-day return where possible.
👪 Fertili
[...]
 fertility treatment.
🐖 Pension - We operate a standard 3% employer contribution and employees auto-contribute 5% of their salary. We use Nest as our provider.
🏡 Local living benefit - A one-off benefit to support living closer to the office: £5,000 if you live within a 30-minute walk, or £2,500 within a 30-minute bike. It is optional, available immediately on signing, and not linked to performance or progression.
🚕 If you choose to work late in the office, you can expense dinner after 7pm and an Uber home after 9pm, or earlier if you feel unsafe travelling in the dark. This is optional and about wellbeing, not performance or expectations.
⛵️And of course, an adventure of a lifetime!
 🌈 Inclusive & Diverse by Design
 We care about building a product that is loved and a culture that is rich in perspectives, experiences, and backgrounds.
Our team represents more than ten different cultures. We come together every lunch time for a home cooked meal, rotated among team members!
We want everyone in our team to know that they belong. We are purposeful about this and are proactively building a company that is inclusive of all people; from race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, neurodiversity, disability, colour, and national origin - essentially every type of diversity. We don’t just want people who fit in, we want them to fit together. We're active in continually improving the way we make this happen.

You will drive the migration of on-premises SQL Server and Oracle estates to AWS managed databases, position AWS's purpose-built database portfolio, and ensure our customers' data foundations are cloud-native, resilient, and AI-ready. You will work on some of EMEAs largest customers and largest deals, partnering closely with our migrations and account teams and partners to land complex, multi-year outcomes. You will also be the voice of EMEA back to the service team, carrying the needs of EMEA customers to our database service teams to help reshape our service and roadmap strategy.
Key job responsibilities
 GTM strategy and execution for AWS Database across EMEA, messaging, positioning, and campaigns for the EMEA areas, with customers from all segments.
 Serve as the EMEA point of contact for all database motions, the connective tissue between Sales Specialists, Specialist SAs, Partner teams, and the area sales teams carrying database quota.
 Win large migrations to AWS, migrate on-premises commercial database estates to AWS managed, purpose-built databases, getting customers ready for AI and agentic workloads.
 Lead engagement on EMEA's largest and most strategic deals, partnering with migrations, commercial/deal, and partner teams to accelerate and close complex, multi-year opportunities.
 Design Scale Sales Motions that drive adoption beyond the top tier, leveraging AWS Field teams, partner channels, and funding levers to unblock deals.

You are the person the field, partners, and customers come to for anything database in EMEA. You operate across the EMEA areas and every segment, building the strategy and executing it, measuring success by the collective growth of the EMEA database business.

TLDR; Conduct's first revenue operations hire. You will build RevOps from scratch: the systems, planning and data our whole go-to-market team runs on, and make it AI-native from day one.
Why Conduct
The world's largest companies compete by being different, and most of that difference lives in the software they've built for themselves, which decides everything from how parcels reach your door to how food gets onto supermarket shelves. That software is a real advantage, but it's also the hardest part of the business to change safely, so good ideas often wait months or even years for the systems to catch up.
Every large enterprise has a software company hiding inside it, and Conduct is building the operating system for it. We read a company's code and processes, work out what needs to change, and help the business and its systems move forward together, wherever custom software has become too complex to change safely.
Fortune Global 500 companies like DHL and Daimler Truck already trust us with their most critical systems, and we've just raised a $60M Series A from Index Ventures, ICONIQ and SAP.
We're a talent-dense team of about 70, growing fast across London and New York, with people from Palantir, G-Research, Legora and Sequoia. Extreme ownership, high velocity, low-ego collaboration. What you build here will shape the company and how the world's largest companies operate.
About the role
Our go-to-market team is growing fast in London and New York, and over the next year we'll scale it several times over, with new account executives and regional directors joining across both offices. They sell a technical product to CIOs and IT leaders at some of the world's largest companies, in long deals with many stakeholders, often alongside partners like SAP and the major consultancies. To grow at that pace, everyone needs one clear picture of the business and an operating rhythm they trust.
Today there's no RevOps function, so you'll be starting from a blank page. You'll decide how we plan, measure and run go-to-market, then build it yourself: the CRM and the systems around it, the planning cycle, the forecast and the analytics that tell leadership where to focus.
We're an AI company, so we expect RevOps to be AI-native too. Agents should do the work that headcount does elsewhere, so a small team can have an outsized impact. You'll work closely with our founders, sales leaders, partnerships, marketing and finance.
What you'll do
 Build the function from scratch. Hire and lead a small founding team, and set one set of definitions, KPIs and data standards across sales, marketing, partnerships and deployment strategy, so the whole company works from a single source of truth.
 Own the GTM tech stack. Implement and run the CRM and the tools around it, with clean data captured at the source rather than fixed after the fact.
 Put agents to work. Design and ship AI workflows for account research, enrichment, routing, pipeline hygiene and forecast inputs, and decide where a human stays in the loop and how the output is checked before anyone acts on it.
 Run the planning cycle. Own territory and coverage design, capacity and headcount planning, quota setting and comp plan design for enterprise land-and-expand deals.
 Run the revenue rhythm. Lead forecast calls, pipeline reviews and QBRs, build a forecast leadership can rely on, and deliver board-ready reporting with the story behind the numbers.
 Set commercial guardrails. Work with our deal desk on pricing discipline, approvals and contracting workflows for complex enterprise and partner deals.
 Decide where we play next. Turn win/loss, conversion and customer data into decisions, size the market by vertical and geography, and build the case and the infrastructure for new markets.
What we're looking for
A track record of building or scaling RevOps at a high-growth B2B software company, ideally one selling complex, technical products to enterprises. You've owned territory design, quota and comp plans, forecasting and pipeline management, and hired the team to run it.
Deep, hands-on CRM expertise (Salesforce or HubSpot at admin level) and experience designing an integrated GTM stack.
AI-native. You've put AI agents or LLM-powered workflows into production for a business team, and can show what broke, what you changed and the impact. Your default is to automate.
Strong analytical skills, including SQL and BI tools, with experience sizing markets and turning data into go-to-market decisions.
Equally strategic and hands-on. You design the system and also build the models, dashboards and workflows yourself.
A clear communicator who earns credibility with sales leaders, founders and the board.
Experience with long enterprise sales cycles, the SAP ecosystem or systems integrator co-sell motions is a strong plus.
An appetite for being in the office every day, close to the team and the work.
Your seniority does not matter. Ambition, craft and the ability to turn ideas into high-quality work quickly do. We sponsor visas from everywhere. We're convinced diverse teams build better products, and we especially encourage people from groups underrepresented in tech to reach out.

 Customer Success Strategy & Leadership

Oversee client health tracking, reporting, and CRM accuracy

li-4490316735.description:
At Moss, we give finance professionals the power to automate their day-to-day and make forward-thinking decisions.
 Our culture is what makes that possible: we play to win, we obsess over quality, and we win as One Moss, and it works. Moss closed a €35 million Series C in August 2026, crossing a €1 billion valuation, and became one of Europe's fintech unicorns. Join us for what's next.
 Moss is scaling fast, and our commercial team is growing with it. That means Revenue Enablement has more exciting projects to deliver in 2027. We are looking for a Revenue Enablement Specialist to join our Revenue Enablement Lead and turn that growth into consistent, repeatable results across our revenue teams.
This is a rare 0 to 1 opportunity. You will build onboarding, training programs and knowledge management, and see them used in the field. You will also help bring AI-enabled workflows into everyday selling.
Maybe you are an experienced enabler who wants something new and adventurous. Maybe you are a seller who wants to turn what works for you into something that helps a whole team win. Either way, you will have real room to build and make an impact. You will report to the Revenue Enablement Lead, sitting within RevOps function and who sets the strategy and KPIs. You will work with xDR and AE teams, and support other commercial teams as priorities change. You will partner with Sales, RevOps , Product, Automation and PMM, so enablement works in the field and its impact can be measured.
 Projects you will work on
Commercial onboarding: Build and run onboarding that helps new hires ramp faster and sell with confidence.
xDR programmes: Deliver enablement programmes for our xDR teams.
Product enablement: Work with the Product enablement team on ad hoc projects, such as getting new features and launches into the field.
 Your Responsibilities
Build the Revenue Enablement foundation: Build and run the core enablement system within the strategy set by the Lead. This includes sales playbooks, onboarding programmes, training cadence and manager-led coaching frameworks.
Drive adoption of AI-enabled workflows: Take existing AI initiatives (e.g. MEDDIC coaching, BDR Coach, knowledge retrieval systems) and make them part of how teams really work. Adoption is the goal.
Embed enablement into the operating rhythm: Bring it into onboarding, weekly team meetings, deal reviews and pipeline management, with support from frontline managers.
Centralise knowledge and enablement tools: Build on one source of truth for GTM content. Set up lightweight tools (call libraries, LMS pilots, structured workflows) with clear ownership, easy search and consistent use.
Track and improve revenue impact: Track and report on the KPIs agreed with RevOps and the Lead (ramp time, win rate, ACV, forecast hygiene, MEDDIC completeness, workflow adoption). Run targeted pilots and improve programmes based on results.
Work independently: Once scope is approved, you deliver from start to finish and manage your own stakeholders.
 About You
3 to 5 years in enablement, RevOps, sales operations or a similar GTM role in high-growth B2B SaaS, or a seller with a strong record of coaching peers.
You use AI tools well to work faster and help GTM teams adopt them.
You can work alone once the goal and scope are clear.
German language skills are a nice to have, not a requirement.
 Skills And Attributes
Builder: You build from zero with clarity and discipline and create repeatable systems (MEDDIC, onboarding, coaching, governance).
Operator: You are practical and focused on revenue outcomes. You turn frameworks into playbooks, rubrics, templates and training that teams use.
Data-driven: You link enablement to measurable impact, run fast pilots and improve based on data.
Cross-functional connector: You work with Sales, PMM, Product, CS and RevOps. You turn field feedback into GTM insights and respect who owns what.
AI and workflow enabler: You are comfortable with AI tools and automation and know how to build them into GTM processes.
Systems thinker: You design knowledge, tools and AI workflows that reduce friction and give people one trusted source of truth without heavy process.
 About Moss
[...]
's mid-sized businesses, giving companies real-time visibility and full control over their spend. By automating card issuing, invoice management and expenses, Moss simplifies financial workflows and frees finance and accounting teams from manual, administrative work.
Founded in Berlin and used by more than 10,000 businesses including Flink, Schufa, n8n and Auto1, Moss has raised €220+ million to date and operates in Germany, the Netherlands, the UK and further EU markets. In August 2026, Moss closed a €35 million Series C led by Portage, crossing a €1 billion valuation and becoming one of Europe's newest fintech unicorns. Moss is backed by investors including Valar Ventures, Tiger Global, Global Founders Capital, Cherry Ventures, A-Star.
We're a team of 300+ people from 50+ nationalities across 5 offices in Europe and we hire, reward, and grow people based on Moss DNA: playing to win, obsessing over quality, winning as One Moss. If that's how you want to work, we want to hear from you. - here's what else to expect:
Top-of-market compensation package, including equity. 
Our vibrant offices are at the heart of our culture, where in-person time fuels collaboration and connection over weekly breakfasts and Friday demos.
Additional benefits include: 20 days “work from abroad”, 600EUR/GBP Learning & Development Budget, and other local benefits.
 Unless stated otherwise, benefits apply to full-time positions (interns and working students receive a tailored package).
 By applying for the above position, you will confirm that you have reviewed and agreed to our Data Privacy Policy .

About the Company 
Spacewell, a Nemetschek Group company, provides smart building and workplace software that helps organisations optimise space, streamline facility operations and create more efficient, people-centric workplaces.
 Your mission 
As a Global Sales Enablement Specialist, you will equip our sales teams worldwide with the knowledge, skills and resources to engage customers effectively. You will combine hands-on training with content management and practical sales guidance, translating complex product information into clear customer value.
Reporting to the Director Sales Support, you will work closely with the Global Sales Enablement Lead and colleagues across Sales, Pre-Sales, Product, Product Marketing and Customer Success.
 What you’ll do 
Develop and deliver sales onboarding and ongoing training, agreeing learning objectives and readiness criteria with sales managers and subject-matter experts.
Create and maintain sales materials and practical playbooks covering product positioning, discovery, qualification, objection handling and best practices.
Manage a central, searchable content library, keeping resources accessible, approved and up to date through clear ownership and version control.
Support RFI and tender processes by providing approved documentation and maintaining the document library. Drafting answers, managing bids and submitting responses remain with the sales or bid owner.
Coordinate enablement priorities and sales readiness for product launches, using learning outcomes, content usage and stakeholder feedback to continuously improve.
 What we’re looking for 
You have 3–5 years of relevant SaaS experience in sales enablement, sales training, sales operations, documentation support or a comparable role.
You combine experience delivering sales onboarding and training with the ability to create engaging sales materials and practical playbooks.
You bring strong organisational skills, experience managing controlled content libraries and familiarity with documentation support for RFI, RFP or tender processes.
You take ownership, collaborate effectively across teams and use data and feedback to prioritise improvements. You are comfortable with CRM, content management, collaboration and content creation tools.
You have strong presentation, facilitation and business-writing skills in Dutch and English, and translate complex information into clear customer benefits.
You are confident using AI-powered tools, such as Perplexity, to research, create and refine sales enablement content, applying sound judgement to ensure accuracy, relevance and quality
You have strong PowerPoint skills and an eye for visual storytelling, turning complex product information into compelling, customer-focused presentations
 Why join Spacewell 
Join an international, innovative team shaping the future of smart, sustainable buildings. You will directly support the development of our global sales teams in a culture built on ownership, teamwork, passion, respect and excellence.
 Our Spacewell benefits 
A full-time contract of 40 hours with flexible working hours
32 days of holiday to recharge and enjoy your free time
A hybrid work model: 2 days a week at our Wilrijk (Antwerp) office, combining collaboration with focus time at home
A company laptop to stay connected wherever you work
Group and medical insurance
Phone subscription
Net allowance
Lunch vouchers (€8 per worked day)
Eco vouchers
Benefits @ Work discounts
Performance-based bonus – because your impact matters
A company car with fuel card, ensuring comfort and mobility
Access to Learning & Development platforms to continue growing your skills
A modern, inspiring office environment that showcases our products and fosters a vibrant team spirit

Hiring: B2B SaaS Go-to-Market Director 
 Location: London, UK (On-site)
 Employment: Full-Time, Permanent
 Domain: PropTech / EdTech / Enterprise SaaS
 About the Role 
We are seeking an accomplished B2B SaaS Go-to-Market Director to lead the 0-to-1 commercial launch of a new enterprise SaaS platform built for university accommodation teams and property management groups.
This role owns the commercial engine from scratch: defining market segmentation and pricing, personally closing the initial wave of institutional enterprise deals, and scaling a high-performing commercial team across the UK and Europe.
 Key Responsibilities 
 GTM Strategy & Pricing: Build and execute the commercial model, pricing architecture, licensing structures, and launch sequencing across UK/EU universities and PBSA operators.
 Direct Enterprise Sales: Personally originate and navigate complex institutional tenders, procurement frameworks, and multi-stakeholder buying committees (estates, accommodation, IT, finance).
 Team & Function Building: Establish the sales playbook, battlecards, and pipeline disciplines from scratch; hire and lead sales, solutions, and customer success functions.
 Ecosystem Partnerships: Represent the company across key industry forums (CUBO, ASRA, ACUHO-I, Unipol) and build strategic integration/channel partnerships.
 What We Are Looking For 
 10+ years of commercial leadership in B2B SaaS with full quota/revenue ownership.
 Must-Have: Direct experience selling enterprise software into universities, Higher Education institutions, or large PBSA / residential property management operators .
Proven ability to close high-value deals within complex, committee-based procurement and tender cycles measured in quarters.
Deep understanding of campus accommodation operations (allocations, inventory, resident experience, estates).
Strong track record building commercial playbooks and teams from the ground up.
 Interested in shaping the next chapter of student living technology?

Description 
Sprout Social is looking to hire a Business Analyst, GTM Systems to the Sales & Customer Experience team.
You’ll be the bridge between our revenue teams and the systems they run on. You’ll turn business needs into clear requirements, make sure what gets built actually works before it reaches the field, and work hand in hand with our Salesforce IT team. You’ll also play a leading role in our CPQ evaluation and in fixing how we measure marketing and pipeline attribution.
 Why join Sprout’s Revenue Operations, Sales & Customer Experience team? 
At Sprout Social, our Sales and Customer Experience team is the driving force behind how today’s most innovative brands use Sprout to power the future of customer connection. We sell and support the leading social intelligence platform for businesses, helping organizations unlock the full value of social data to drive strategic decisions. Through powerful social intelligence and trusted partnership, we enable teams to build authentic relationships and drive meaningful business impact.
As the strategic engine of our go-to-market organization, Revenue Operations builds the infrastructure that turns data into action. We specialize in architecting world-class processes and delivering the operational clarity that allows our teams to move with speed, anticipate market shifts, and optimize the entire customer lifecycle for sustainable growth.
In this role, you will collaborate with the brightest minds in the industry to support global giants like Salesforce, Airbnb, and Equifax. Just as importantly, we believe in the power of our people. You’ll find a culture that honors your ambition, encourages you to explore new horizons, and provides the framework for you to build a career that matters. If you’re ready to champion innovation and accelerate your impact, this is where you can do your best work.
 What you’ll do 
Partner with Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, Renewals and Deal Desk to turn business needs into clear requirements, user stories and acceptance criteria.
Own intake and prioritization for GTM systems requests, working with the Director of GTM Systems & Applied AI and Salesforce IT to maintain a single, prioritized backlog.
Plan and run user acceptance testing, triage defects, and secure business-owner sign-off before changes reach the field.
Write release notes and field communications, and support reps and managers through changes.
Lead requirements, scenario design and scoring for our CPQ evaluation, and support delivery of the CPQ roadmap.
Define and fix marketing and pipeline attribution: requirements, source data capture in Salesforce, and validated reporting that Marketing and Sales both trust.
Monitor data quality on forecast, renewals and source fields, find root causes, and keep data and process definitions documented.
Use AI tools to draft, test and document, and spend your own time on judgment, review and decisions.
 What you’ll bring 
You know how revenue teams work and how to get the right thing built. You write requirements that engineers can build from, you’re rigorous about testing, and you earn trust with everyone from a frontline rep to a VP.
The minimum qualifications for this role include:
4+ years of experience in business analysis, systems analysis or sales operations, supporting a B2B SaaS go-to-market team.
Hands-on Salesforce experience and a working understanding of the data model.
Proven ability to gather business requirements and write user stories and acceptance criteria.
Experience planning and running UAT and managing releases with a central IT team that owns
